title: Pathways for students who leave school before completing national certifications
asked: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked what alternative education, training or reintegration pathways the Ministry of Education provides for students required to leave school before completing their national certifications, so they are not left without viable progression options.
response: Mr David Neo said the goal is for all Singaporeans to have education, training or reintegration pathways through life. Students who wish to continue education can approach their last school or MOE's Education and Career Guidance Centre; if assessed age-appropriate for re-admission, they can enrol in a secondary school, which may provide bridging programmes. Alternative options include the ITE General Education programme for adult learners to obtain GCE N or O Levels, then Higher Nitec and Diploma programmes, and SkillsFuture Singapore subsidies for industry-relevant training. In supplementary answers, he described early upstream intervention, individual tracking, school counsellors, parent engagement, community partners, and said MOE tracks outcomes while students are in the school system but not after they leave, with other indicators from manpower statistics, SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore.

key_points.point: Goal is for all Singaporeans to have education, training or reintegration pathways through life.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: it is our goal for all Singaporeans to have education, training or reintegration pathways through life

key_points.point: Students who wish to continue education may approach the school in which they were last enrolled.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: those who wish to continue their education may approach the school in which they were last enrolled

key_points.point: They can also approach MOE's Education and Career Guidance Centre for advice on suitable educational pathways.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: they can approach the Ministry of Education's Education and Career Guidance Centre for advice and guidance on suitable educational pathways

key_points.point: If assessed age-appropriate for re-admission, they can be enrolled at a secondary school.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: If they are assessed to be age-appropriate for re-admission, they can be enrolled at a secondary school.

key_points.point: Receiving schools may assess students and provide bridging programmes for transition back to mainstream education.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: The receiving schools may assess these students and provide bridging programmes to smoothen their transition back into mainstream education.

key_points.point: Students with minimal academic qualifications can consider the ITE General Education programme.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: students with minimal academic qualifications can consider the Institute of Technical Education General Education programme

key_points.point: The ITE General Education programme allows adult learners to obtain GCE N or O Levels.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: which allows adult learners to obtain their GCE "N" or "O" Levels

key_points.point: This can lead to Higher Nitec and Diploma programmes in institutes of higher learning.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: This, in turn, then allows them to subsequently enrol in Higher Nitec and Diploma programmes in our institutes of higher learning.

key_points.point: SkillsFuture Singapore provides subsidies for a wide range of industry-relevant training programmes.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: SkillsFuture Singapore also provides subsidies for a wide range of industry-relevant training programmes

key_points.point: Students showing signs of disengagement are individually tracked and supported.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: once any of our students show any signs of disengagement, they are individually tracked and they are supported

key_points.point: Form teachers and school counsellors reach out to students to address challenges.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: Form teachers and school counsellors reach out to our students to understand and to address any of these challenges.

key_points.point: Efforts are made to counsel and dissuade at-risk students from dropping out, including engaging parents.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: every effort is made to counsel and to dissuade these at-risk students from dropping out of school, including engaging their parents

key_points.point: MOE provides resources and guidance for schools to create a supportive school environment.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: the Ministry of Education (MOE) also provides resources and guidance for schools to create a supportive school environment

key_points.point: Students may be referred to school-based programmes with befriending or mentoring by community partners and volunteers.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: students are also referred to school-based programmes where they can be engaged through befriending or mentoring by community partners and volunteers

key_points.point: Schools work with community partners and agencies such as ComLink+, self-help groups and social service agencies.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: Schools also work very closely with community partners and Government agencies, such as the Ministry of Social and Family Development's ComLink+, self-help groups, social service agencies

key_points.point: MOE tracks outcomes of students while they are in the school education system, but not after they leave.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: today, MOE tracks outcomes of students. But once they are not in the school education system anymore, we do not track those further.

key_points.point: Other indicators come from manpower statistics and work by SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: as part of our manpower statistics, as part of what SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore are doing, we do have some of the other indicators

left_open: Specific numbers of students who leave before completing national certifications and successfully transition into alternative education, training or employment pathways.
Whether there are plans to strengthen early identification and intervention beyond the existing measures described.
Additional support for students who struggle to reintegrate after leaving the school system.
supplementary: Early identification and intervention, coordination with family and community partners, and tracking outcomes for students who leave before completing national certifications.
